title: The verifier side of speculative window decoding: a predictability bracket, a machine-checked blast-radius bound, and a decoder-agnostic recover loop
summary: Speculative window decoders hide quantum error-correction decoder latency by guessing the cross-boundary decisions that link adjacent decoding windows, running downstream work on the guess, and verifying lazily. SWIPER and ARTERY each build one predictor, about 90% accurate; neither built the verifier side. We build it on a reconstructed SWIPER harness (Stim rotated surface code, minimum-weight matching). A predictor-only bracket shows the cross-boundary decision is local, the achievable accuracy reaching about 0.999 within three rounds, with small, diffuse headroom over SWIPER. We establish…
